overlap_rationale:
All 12 complete authorized demonstrations are retained, including initial holds, release, retreat and terminal settling. Segments are half-open action intervals [start,stop), with observations [start,stop] inclusive. Each listed endpoint was inspected. Two skills recur for red and blue; they are not color-specific policies. The first acquire occurrence requests red with no predecessor; the second requests blue with red as predecessor. The first deliver occurrence delivers red with blue as the next object; the second delivers blue with no next object. These role IDs are explicit policy-call parameters, supplied by a task-level caller using the named objects/goals, not an oracle timestep. Only red-then-blue execution is demonstrated; reversed order and alternative scheduling remain untested.

There are two intentionally different shared transitions. Acquire-to-deliver overlaps include open-finger final descent, closure and its physical lag, initial lift, high lift and the onset of horizontal transport. Their widths are 103-117 actions (5.15-5.85 s at 20 Hz), not a short tail after grasp. Deliver-to-next-acquire overlaps begin while red is still grasped and descending over its pad, and include finishing the descent, opening, settling, vertical retreat and the high approach toward blue. Their widths are 154-163 actions (7.70-8.15 s). Thus the next acquire policy learns to finish the predecessor's manipulation before approaching its requested object. Delivery learns both pre-grasp takeover and post-release movement toward the next object. The core identities remain acquisition of a requested block and delivery of an acquired block; these wider bridges are part of their interfaces, not independent copies of the entire task. No triple overlap is used.

Boundaries are supported by states rather than a shared episode clock. In demo10000, the acquire exits at 185 and 585 have lifted objects at z=0.2796 and 0.2812 m with horizontal movement beginning; in demo10003 the corresponding exits are 181 and 571, and in demo10011 they are 192 and 584. Red-to-blue bridge entries vary from z=0.126 m in demo10011/272 to z=0.253 m in demo10005/265, with red goal-aligned and fingers still near 0.0183 m each. Bridge exits range from a moving high approach in demo10003/409 (TCP y=0.153 m, blue y=0.214 m) to the blue overhead region in demo10011/435 (TCP z=0.266 m). Supported entry states therefore include incomplete release, rising empty grippers, ongoing high approach, closing fingers and partially lifted blocks, rather than one exact cut pose. Low lateral sweeps with a still-grasped predecessor, off-pad descent, slipped grasps and recovery from spatial/contact errors are not established by temporal overlap.

Common implementation contract for all six independently trained Diffusion Policy candidates: use the supplied synchronized state fields and original eight action channels at 20 Hz. qpos[0:7] and absolute arm targets are Panda joint radians; qpos[7:9] are finger metres, not gripper-command units. qvel uses rad/s and m/s respectively. tcp_pose, red_pose and blue_pose are world metre/wxyz poses; goals are world metres. Action gripper_command is dimensionless: finger target = 0.015 + 0.025*command m, so -1 requests -0.01 m even though a successful grasp has measured fingers near +0.0183 m. Never replace demonstrated targets with measured future qpos: servo lag is real. Use the single observation/action normalizer fitted to the complete, unduplicated original demonstrations, never per-skill statistics. Derived geometric quantities are computed in physical units and scaled with the corresponding original position/velocity scales, without fitting new per-skill ranges. Ignore the two fixed-zero drawer compatibility channels. Representative front images were inspected to verify the two cubes, separate pads, top-down grasps and unobstructed tabletop; these hypotheses use the supplied state poses rather than assume a calibrated image-to-world estimator.

Keep raw segment data unchanged. Future event, waypoint and outcome labels described below are implementation-stage training annotations only. Sample causal histories and action chunks inside the relevant segment; pad/mask missing history or future rather than bridge unrelated occurrences. Split evaluation by original trajectory before making overlapping windows so duplicated transition actions cannot leak across train/validation. Balance occurrences when evaluating learning hypotheses and report core and overlap performance separately. Deployment timing, observation noise, task-level scheduling and availability of additional robot models are unspecified; no unprovided IK, force sensor, simulator rollout or recovery dataset is assumed.

Completion is the supplied conjunction of red_at_goal and blue_at_goal at one observation: all rotated object XY corners must fit their own 0.06 m half-width pads and centre z must be within 0.011 m of 0.02 m. There is no required release, clearance, velocity threshold or sustained hold. For example, demo10000/690 already has blue z=0.02284 m near its goal while gripper_command is still -1, and red is on its pad. Release and retreat are nevertheless retained to teach usable noninterfering interfaces. Final inspected observations in every trajectory have both blocks on their respective pads, fingers near 0.04 m and TCP near z=0.299 m. Readiness criteria stronger than the task contract below are policy-interface hypotheses, not extra success requirements. All claimed learning/generalization benefits are hypotheses until implementation and controlled evaluation.
